---
title: "Layout"
---

Ribasim does not use the location of nodes and the geometry of links in the simulation.
But a model that follows the real water system is much easier to review, on the map and in the [model viewer](../viewer.qmd), so the regional models and the coupled model get a shared layout step.
None of this changes the results.

::: {layout-ncol=2}
![The input model, with straight links.](https://s3.deltares.nl/ribasim-nl/doc-image/figures/level-3-input-model.png){fig-alt="Coloured Basin areas with straight links."}

![The final model, with links along the watercourses, and Junctions where they join.](https://s3.deltares.nl/ribasim-nl/doc-image/figures/level-4-forcing.png){fig-alt="The same area, with links that follow the watercourses."}
:::

## Routing the links

At the end of the forcing stage, `ribasim_nl.network_snapping.snap_model` aligns the layout of the level controlled models with the hydro-objects in `verwerkt/profielen/network.gpkg`, which are written by the [profile generation](profile-generation.qmd):

- Connector nodes stay at the location of the structure they represent.
- Basin nodes are moved onto the nearest main route of the longest connected part of the hydro-objects in their basin, as in the gravity controlled models.
- Links between a Basin and a connector node follow the hydro-objects, complemented by the Top10NL water lines. Hydro-objects are only connected where there is evidence: the culverts (`duikersifonhevel`) of the crossings data, gaps of at most 2 m, and gaps across BGT water surfaces. Connector nodes far from the hydro-objects are connected over the BGT water surfaces, crossing at most 100 m of land.
- Links stay straight if no such route is found, or if it is not less than `ribasim_nl.link_geometries.MAX_STRAIGHT_LINE_RATIO` times longer than the straight line, the same threshold as for the gravity controlled models.

In the gravity controlled models, `snap_to_waterways` routes the links that are still straight along the Top10NL waterways, at the end of their dynamic stage.

## Tidying

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  a["Route links"] --> b["junctionify<br>merge shared parts<br>of links"]
  b --> c["tidy_layout"]
```

`ribasim_nl.junctionify` merges the shared parts of links into Junctions, and `ribasim_nl.layout.tidy_layout` makes sure no nodes are on top of each other and no links overlap.

The inflows and outflows of a Basin share one Junction tree, so each waterway is drawn once, see `ribasim_nl.flow_paths.merge_basin_trees`.
The trees are merged after the last nodes are added to a model, so only the IDs of Junctions change.
Ribasim connects a group of Junctions with one Basin as a neighbour with that Basin, in the direction of the link of each other neighbour with the group, see [Junction](https://ribasim.org/reference/node/junction.html).
The direction of the links within the tree, and with the Basin, does not change the simulation, only the sign of their flow, see `ribasim_nl.flow_paths.towards_basin`.
A link that only carries inflows points towards the Basin, and one that only carries outflows away from it.
A link that carries both follows the main flow: the direction in which the waterway lines it follows are digitized, where they cover most of it, such as the network of Rijkswaterstaat.
Elsewhere it points to the side that can drain the most, in the `afvoer` control state, where ManningResistances and placeholder capacities are unlimited.
`ribasim_nl.flow_paths.Routes` follows the links through Junctions in the same way as Ribasim.

- Bergend Basins are placed 100 m from their doorgaand Basin.
- Nodes that are still within 10 m of each other are moved apart.
- Links that still overlap, such as those of neighbouring Basins along a shared waterway, are offset 5 m.

The gravity controlled models get the same layout step at the end of their dynamic stage, and `ribasim_nl.validation.validate_model` checks it.
It also checks that the Basin areas are valid and have no slivers: parts and holes that are on average at most 1 mm wide, which draw as lines on the map.
`Model.clean_basin_area` fixes both in the regional models and the Rijkswaterstaat model.
The [coupling](couple.qmd) tidies the links between models in the same way, and first rebuilds the routes of the Basins of Rijkswaterstaat along Top10NL, as the Rijkswaterstaat model does, see `ribasim_nl.flow_paths.rebuild_rws_junction_trees`.
In the IJsselmeer, Markermeer, IJmeer and Gouwzee, the network of Rijkswaterstaat only has a few straight lines, so there the routes follow the fairways of OpenStreetMap ([#1010](https://github.com/Deltares/Ribasim-NL/issues/1010)).
Nodes on the shore branch off straight from the nearest point of a fairway from which the line crosses at most 100 m of land, and nodes close together share such a line.
